segments.translation: Utsotanv(i) - it was in afterbirth. It’s still inside the cow. I would wait two or three days for it to pass on its own. But sometimes it won’t do it itself, then I have to take it inside. Then I get a long glove. When you find it, just like the buttons that are here [gestures], there’s a button there [gestures]. [inside cow] And that’s what you have to find. When you take them off, then you can pull it out. I have some medicine and I just put it in there, and the cow gets alright. Sometimes, that ‘breedback’ that they do, they would wait a little longer if that happens. I don’t know why.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏴ,’Ꭱ … ᏥᏥᎾᏝᎥ … ᏍᏊ’Ꭱ ᏕᏥᎾᏝᎥ ᏍᎪ--ᎡᎵᏭ’ᏛᎡᏃ ᏍᎩᎦᏚ ᎾᏕᏘᏱ ᎨᎲ’ᏃᏢ … ᏧᎵᏬᏨ Ꮎ ᎠᎩᎾ, Ꮎ … Ꮟ ᎦᎸ Ꮎ ᏩᎧ, … ᎯᏲᎵᎬ, Ꮎ Marty?
segments.transliteration: ayv,’e … tsitsinatlav … squu’e detsinatlav sgo--eliwu’dveno sgigadu nadetiyi gehv’notlv … tsuliwotsv na agina, na … si galv na waka, … hiyoligv, na Marty?
segments.translation: Me, when I had cows, it was probably about 15 years ago, the calf died while it was still inside the mother. You know Marty?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Yeah. Marty Horn?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏍᎩᎾ, Charles “ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ,’Ꭱ ᏂᎬᏁᎸᎾ, ᏱᎨᎮᏍᏗ, Ꮎ’Ꭱ-Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᏍᏊ ᏩᎧ ᏓᏣᏲᎱᏎᎵ,” Ꭼ-ᎬᏬᎮᎸ … ᎤᏴᏟ’Ꮕ, ᎫᏘᎲ ᏍᎩ’Ꭱ ᏧᏂᎷᏨ Marty Jim-Ꭲ’Ꮕ, Ꮎ’Ꮕ Charles ᏍᎩ’Ꭱ … ᏧᏂᎴᏒ Ꮎ ᏩᎧ, ᎠᏂ-ᎠᏂᎬᎭᎷᏍᎬ ᎭᏫᏂ, ᏗᏢ ᏧᏂᎾ,ᏌᏁᎲ ᎬᏩᎦ,Ꮧ, ᏥᎦᏥᏄᎸᏅ ᎦᏥ--ᎨᏥᏈᏴᎡᏗ
segments.transliteration: vv sgina, Charles “gohu,sdi,’e nigvnelvna, yigehesdi, na’e-na’e squu waka datsayohuseli,” gv-gvwohelv … uyvtli’nv, gutihv sgi’e tsunilutsv Marty Jim-i’nv, na’nv Charles sgi’e … tsunilesv na waka, ani-anigvhalusgv hawini, ditlv tsunina,sanehv gvwaga,di, tsigatsinulvnv gatsi--getsiquiyvedi
segments.translation: Yeah, him and Charles. “If you don’t do anything with that calf, you’re gonna lose the mother, too,” they told me. It was real cold and snowing out. Then they showed up; Marty, Jim, and Charles. They took out the calf, they cut it up while it was still inside and they pulled it out. They wouldn’t let me pay them.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Yeah, yeah, Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ’Ꮫ ᏚᏂᎬᏩᎶ,Ꮩ ᏄᏓᎵᎭ Ꮎ Vet[ernarian] “Call” ᏂᎬᏁ,Ꮧ ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᎣᏂ “call” ᏥᎾᏮᏁᎸ Vet. ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏍᎪᎯ--… Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ‘Ꮩ--ᎠᏮᎨᏩ,Ꮜ, Ꮪ-…ᏚᎬᏩᏠᏅ ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, “ᎠᏮᏌ’Ꮫ ᏗᏩᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᏗ” ᏣᏩᏓᏙ--…ᏣᏪᎵᏒ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᏌᏭ ᏐᏈᎵ, ᏥᏴᏓ, ᏍᏊ ᏙᏳ,’Ꭱ Ꮭ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏙᏨ,--ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, ᎡᎰ’Ꮽ, Ꮎ’Ꮕ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, ᏧᎸᏉ,Ꮧ, ᏐᏈᎵ, ᎤᏛᏒ ᏐᏈᎵ, ᏓᎩᎸᏗᎲ ᎣᏣ--ᎾᏅ ᎤᏍᏗᎧᏂ, ᎠᏧᏣ, ᏍᏊ Ꮎ college ᏥᏓᏕᎶ,ᏆᎲ ᎤᎾ Connor’s Ꮎ Rodeo Team—Rodeo Team ᏥᎨᎸ ᏍᏊ Ꮷ-- ᎤᏩᏌ, ᎤᏤᎵ ᏐᏈᎵ, Ꮎ … Steer—Steer Roping ᏣᎾ,ᏗᎲ ᏗᏛᏁᎯ, Ꮵ’ᎡᎲ ᏍᎩᏃ ᏥᏚᏍᏆᏛ ᎠᏴ, ᏥᏰᎶᎲ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) Ꮭ ‘ᎸᏢ ᏰᏙᎰ ᏃᏭ,
segments.transliteration: Yeah, yeah, tsi,quisdi’dv dunigvwalo,do nudaliha na Vet[ernarian] “Call” nigvne,di ayv, hena, oni “call” tsinawvnelv Vet. squu sgina sgohi--… tla squu yawanv,ta, ‘do--awvgewa,sa, du-…dugvwatlonv ‘ahena, “awvsa’dv diwadelo,quasdi” tsawadado--…tsawelisv (uyetsi,sgv) sawu soquili, tsiyvda, squu doyu,’e tla gohu,sdi, dotsv,--doyu, hena, eho’wu, na’nv agi,sdayvhvsgi, tsulvquo,di, soquili, udvsv soquili, dagilvdihv otsa--nanv usdikani, atsutsa, squu na college tsidadelo,quahv una Connor’s na Rodeo Team—Rodeo Team tsigelv squu tsu-- uwasa, utseli soquili, na … Steer—Steer Roping tsana,dihv didvnehi, tsi’ehv sgino tsidusquadv ayv, tsiyelohv (uniyetsi,sgv) tla ‘lvtlv yedoho nowu,
segments.translation: Yeah, it does cost a lot to call the vet. The last time I had to call the vet. I can’t remember how much it cost me. “I have to learn it myself,” I thought. I also have a horse, but it’s just there. My wife likes horses. She grew up riding horses. Our youngest boy, he was going to college at Conner’s. He was on the Rodeo Team. He had his own horse. He was doing the Steer-Roping. He graduated and then I was feeding it. [laughs] He don’t go anywhere anymore. [the horse]

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: The horse?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Is he still a good horse to ride?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Oh, yeah! ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, ᏥᏥᏂ,ᏗᏅ’Ꮫ ᏃᏭ ᏃᏭ ᏐᎢ, ᏐᏈᎵ, ᏃᏭ,
segments.transliteration: Oh, yeah! ‘ahena, tsitsini,dinv’dv nowu nowu soi, soquili, nowu,
segments.translation: Oh, yeah! I sold him, though. But there’s another one.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Is the other one good to ride?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Ꮵ’ᎡᎲ Ꭰ’ᎠᏴᎳᎩ,’Ꮫ ᏃᏭ, ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, ᎤᏓᏅ,Ꮨ,
segments.transliteration: tsi’ehv a’ayvlagi,’dv nowu, doyu, hena, udanv,ti,
segments.translation: It was, but it’s getting old now. It is really tame.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏳᏓᎭ ᎠᏩᏚᎵᎰ ᏐᏉᎵ, ᎤᏓᏅ,Ꮨ ᏱᎩ, Charlie Ꮎ … Ꮟ ᎠᏩᏚᎵ Ꮎ ᎠᎩᏅᎪᏫ,ᏥᏓᏍᏗ ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏍᏓᏱ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏩᏛᏗ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏓᏅ,Ꮨ ᎤᏔᎾ,’ᎮᎾ, ᏍᏊ--ᎡᏆ ᎮᎾ, ᏔᏈᏴᎯ,
segments.transliteration: yudaha awaduliho soquoli, udanv,ti yigi, Charlie na … si awaduli na aginvgowi,tsidasdi tsanv,ta, sdayi squu awadvdi sgi yudanv,ti utana,’hena, squu--equa hena, taquiyvhi,
segments.translation: Sometimes I want a horse that is tame, Charlie. Cause I still want to get out and about. It’s hard to find a good horse. You have to pay a lot.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Yeah, children used to ride our horse.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: When you were growing up, did you all plant a garden?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎥᎥ yeah, yeah, ᏂᎪᎯᎸ’Ꮫ … Mom ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎠᏫᏒᏍᎬ, ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: vv yeah, yeah, nigohilv’dv … Mom nigohilv awisvsgv, tsigehv
segments.translation: Yeah, all the time. Mom always planted a garden.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did she can the food and put it up?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏥᎨᎲ ‘Ꮧ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏄᏛᏃ … ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏱᎩ, … ᎣᏓᏭᏖᏍᏗ(46:20) ᎭᏗ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, Ꮒ-ᏂᏣᏛᏁ ᏥᎨᎰ ᎾᎮᎾ, ᏙᎦᎳᏑᏢᎾ, ᎮᎾ, Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, … Ꮭ ᏲᎦᏍᎪᎵ,ᏓᏁᎲ ᏦᎦᎳᏑᏢ,Ꮧ ᏐᎭᏫᏂ, ᏃᏭ, Ᏹ-ᏱᏙᏧᏖ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏱᏥᏯᏛᏛᏅ Mama ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, ᏃᏣᏛᏁᎲ ᏂᎦᏪᏍᎬ ᏙᏧᏖᏍᎬ ᏄᎾ, yeah, Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ,’Ꭱ ᎣᏥᏫᏒᏍᎬ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᏔᎩ’Ꮕ, ᏍᏊ ᎤᏩᏌ, ᏙᏥᎯᎲ … wring-wringing their necks? ᎣᏍᏓ, Ꮒ-ᏱᏂᎦᏛᎦ, Ꮵ’ᎡᎲ Ꮟ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏓᏁᎸ ᏥᏫᏒᏍᎪ … ᏂᎪᎯᎸ
segments.transliteration: vv tsigehv ‘di yawanv,ta, nudvno … osda, yigi, … odawutesdi(46:20) hadi yawanv,ta, ni-nitsadvne tsigeho nahena, dogalasutlvna, hena, tla hena, … tla yogasgoli,danehv tsogalasutlv,di sohawini, nowu, yi-yidotsute tla ilvhiyu yitsiyadvdvnv Mama ‘ahena, notsadvnehv nigawesgv dotsutesgv nuna, yeah, tsi,quisdi,’e otsiwisvsgv tsigehv tsitagi’nv, squu uwasa, dotsihihv … wring-wringing their necks? osda, ni-yinigadvga, tsi’ehv si’dv squu adanelv tsiwisvsgo … nigohilv
segments.translation: Yeah, she did. I don’t know, but when the potatoes got ripe enough for us to go pick up, I don’t know what you all did, but we had to take our shoes off. She didn’t allow us to wear shoes in the garden. We’d pick them out of the ground. I never asked Mama, we just did what she said. We were picking potatoes. Yeah, we planted a lot. We also killed chickens ourselves. Wringing their necks, I could do that well by myself. I still plant a garden at the house all the time.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Do you still can and put them away?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Ꮭ’Ᏺ ᏃᏭ, ᏥᎨᎲ’Ꭱ ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, ᏣᏁᎲ ᎣᎩᏅᏌ’Ꮽ ᎨᎰ ᎠᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, ᎤᏕᏙᎰ ᏄᏓᎵᎭ ᎤᏓᏍᏓᏴᏗ, ᎣᏍᏗᏔᎵ’Ꮽ, ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, Ꮟ’ᎡᏲ Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ, ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎬ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎪ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ,
segments.transliteration: tla’yo nowu, tsigehv’e ‘ahena, tsanehv oginvsa’wu geho adanelv agi,sdayvhvsgi, udedoho nudaliha udasdayvdi, osditali’wu, ‘ahena, si’eyo tsi,quisdi, adasdayvhvsgv, osda, adasdayvhvsgo agi,sdayvhvsgi,
segments.translation: Not anymore. I used to, because back then, the kids were home. And now it’s just me and my wife. It bothers her sometimes just to cook for the two of us. Still, yet, she cooks a lot. She’s a good cook, my wife.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎾᎾ ᏏᏆ, ᏥᏓᏂᎯᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᎯᏗ, ᎦᎪ,’Ꭱ ᎨᎮ ᏏᏆ, ᏥᏚᎾᏝᎥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᎯᏗ?
segments.transliteration: nana siqua, tsidanihiho tsigehv gohidi, gago,’e gehe siqua, tsidunatlav tsigehv gohidi?
segments.translation: How about the hogs they used to kill long time ago, who had hogs back then?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s how it was.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏙᏳ, ᏦᏎᎰ ᏱᏚᏂᏒᏍᏔᎾ, ᏏᏆ, ᎠᎯᏍᏗ ᏚᏯ’Ꮕ, ᏱᏚᏂᏙᏓ, Ꮎ’Ꮕ, Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᏳᏂ-ᏳᏂᏝᏅ’Ꮽ ‘Ᏺ ᎭᏫᏯ ᏳᏂᎬᎭᎷᏯ, ᎤᎾ ᏍᏊ ᏥᏩᏅᏂᏍᏗᎲ
segments.transliteration: doyu, tsoseho yidunisvstana, siqua, ahisdi duya’nv, yidunidoda, na’nv, na’nv, yuni-yunitlanv’wu ‘yo hawiya yunigvhaluya, una squu tsiwanvnisdihv
segments.translation: It used to be good when they made plans to kill a hog. Then when they would warm up the beans and cut up the meat, they’d just cook it right there, too.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: They would just cook it right there.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: That’s when you knew you really were going to eat, right?!

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: You sure did!

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Do you miss that type of cooking?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: I sure do!

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: Ꮟ ᎠᎩᏒᎪ ᎠᏴ, ᏳᏓᎭ ᏧᎦ,ᏒᏍᏗ, ᏯᏒᎦ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏓ--ᏙᏱ, ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴᏅ
segments.transliteration: si agisvgo ayv, yudaha tsuga,svsdi, yasvga, tsigehv ada--doyi, adasdayvnv
segments.translation: I can still smell that smoke like it was back then. Especially cooking outside.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Ꮎ smokehouse ᏙᎲ? ᏂᎦᏛᏁᎰ ᎠᏮᏌ,’Ᏺ ᏕᏥᎦ,ᏒᏍᏗᎰ ᎭᏫᏯ ᎦᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎪ ᏙᏱ ᏳᏓᎭ ᏄᏓᎵᎭ … ᎠᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮧ,’ᏛᏲ ᏙᏱ, … ᎠᎩᏯᎸᏍᏗ ᏓᏬᎵ, ᎪᏧᎾ, ᏒᎩ, ᏜᏱᏕ ᏂᎦᏓ, … ᎾᎮᎾ, Ꮎ Maryetta ᏧᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏯᎩ,ᏑᎵ,ᎪᏣ,’Ꮓ ᏥᏕ--… ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, … ᏫᏕᏥᏯᏂᎰ Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᏗᎾ,ᏕᏲᎲᏍᎩ, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏙᏧ--ᏍᎩ’Ꮽ ᏥᏃᏣᏛᏁᎲ
segments.transliteration: na smokehouse dohv? nigadvneho awvsa,’yo detsiga,svsdiho hawiya gadasdayvhvsgo doyi yudaha nudaliha … agilvquo,di,’dvyo doyi, … agiyalvsdi dawoli, gotsuna, svgi, dlayide nigada, … nahena, na Maryetta tsuna,delo,quasdi tsigehv tsidagilvwi,sdanehv yagi,suli,gotsa,’no tside--… diniyotli, … widetsiyaniho na’nv, dina,deyohvsgi, nigada, dotsu--sgi’wu tsinotsadvnehv
segments.translation: The smokehouse, ain’t it? I do it myself, I smoke meat. I cook outside every now and again. I like to go hunt for things outside, like mushrooms, Kochun, wild onion, and poke salad. I used to work at Maryetta School. When I got off work, I’d go get the children and the teachers, too. That’s what we did.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You all went looking for mushrooms?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᏓᏬᎵ, ᏜᏱᏙ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏒᎩ, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᏍᎩᎾ Ᏺ’ᎤᏖᏌ, ᏗᎾ,--ᏗᎾ,ᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏂᏓᏅᏁᎲ ᏣᏂ’ᎢᏍᎬ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, Ꭲ’ᎠᏓ, ᎮᎾ, Ꮭ ᏳᎾᏅ,Ꮫ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ,’Ꭱ program Cherokee Nation ᏥᏄᏅᏅ ᎢᎾ
segments.transliteration: dawoli, dlayido’le yigi, svgi, nigada, nowu’nv, sgina yo’utesa, dina,--dina,dasdayvhvsgi, osda, nidanvnehv tsani’isgv diniyotli, tla hena, i’ada, hena, tla yunanv,dv yusdi, gehv gohu,sdi,’e program Cherokee Nation tsinunvnv ina
segments.translation: Yeah, mushrooms and poke and wild onion. Everything. When we found some, the cooks there would clean it and cook it. The children ate it and they didn’t know what it was. It was a program the Cherokee Nation had, I don’t know what it was.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Oh, something like “culture” class?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎥᎥ culture ᎤᏖᏗ, ᎨᎵᎲ ᏥᎾᎾ,ᏛᏁᎲ … Ꮎ’Ꮕ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ, ᏥᏲᎵᎦ, ᏥᏯᏘᏁᎲ ᏍᏊ Ꮎ arrowheads ᏕᎪᏢᏍᎪ … Ꮎ Arkansas-Ꭲ ᏗᏢ, Ꮒ,ᏓᏳᎶᏒ ᏳᎾᎦ,ᏙᏍᏗ, ᏕᎪᏢᏍᎬ ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮧ, ᎮᎾ, ᏍᎩᎾᎾ Ꮎ … Ꮎ Hickory Chicken ᏣᏃᏎᎰ ᏃᏭ, ᏥᎩ, ᎮᎾ, … well, … ᎠᏮᎨᏩ,ᏍᎪ’Ꮫ ᏃᏭ, today’s Thursday ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: vv culture utedi, gelihv tsinana,dvnehv … na’nv asgaya, tsiyoliga, tsiyatinehv squu na arrowheads degotlvsgo … na Arkansas-i ditlv, ni,dayulosv yunaga,dosdi, degotlvsgv ayv, hena, agilvquo,di, hena, sginana na … na Hickory Chicken tsanoseho nowu, tsigi, hena, … well, … awvgewa,sgo’dv nowu, today’s Thursday dohv?
segments.translation: Yeah, a culture class. I thought they were doing real good. And then I brought in a guy I know who makes arrowheads. He came from Arkansas for them to watch him make them. I liked that one that they call “Hickory Chicken” well, I forget today’s Thursday, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Yeah, Nvgine(i) Ig(a) – Thursday.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ‘Ꮲ ᎮᎾ, Ꮎ--‘Ꮲ ᎮᎾ, Ꮎ ᏩᏁᎢ, ᎠᏏᏛ ᏱᎾᎵ,ᏍᏓ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: ‘tlv hena, na--‘tlv hena, na wanei, asidv yinali,sda dohv?
segments.translation: You can find them growing anywhere on an old hickory log (that’s laying horizontal).

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏃᏭ’Ꮫ Ꮎ ᏓᎩᏩᏛᎲ last… Friday-Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏓᎩᏩᏛᎲ Hickory Chicken ᏓᎩᏃᏢ ᏦᏍᏓ, Ꮒ,ᏚᏮᏁᎸ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, Sunday-Ꮫ ᏙᏓᏩᏍᎬ ᎨᎵ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᎩᏂᎬ ᎠᏴ, … Stump ᎤᎾᏭ ‘ᏓᏁᎸ Ꭰ’ᎥᏱ ᏗᏢ Ꮎ ᏐᎢ, ᏤᏡ,Ꭼ ᎥᎾ Ꭰ’ᎢᎴᏴᏍᏔᏅ ᎤᎾ ᏧᎾᎦ,ᏌᏔᏅ ᎤᎾ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᏥᏂ,ᏓᏮᏅ,ᏕᏒ Ꮎ ᎤᏍᏗᎧᏂ, ᎠᏧᏣ, ᏍᏊ ᏥᏚ-ᏥᏚᏃᏢ ᏥᏚᏩᏛᎲ … Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᎫᎫ ᏍᏊ ᏕᏥᎾᏩ,ᏘᎰ ᏃᏭ ᏥᎩ, ᎮᎾ, ᏕᎦᎾᏩ,Ꮧ,
segments.transliteration: vv nowu’dv na dagiwadvhv last… Friday-dv tsigehv dagiwadvhv Hickory Chicken daginotlv tsosda, ni,duwvnelv agi,sdayvhvsgi, Sunday-dv dodawasgv geli tsigehv doginigv ayv, … Stump unawu ‘danelv a’vyi ditlv na soi, tsetlu,gv vna a’ileyvstanv una tsunaga,satanv una (uyetsi,sgv) tsini,dawvnv,desv na usdikani, atsutsa, squu tsidu-tsidunotlv tsiduwadvhv … na’nv, gugu squu detsinawa,tiho nowu tsigi, hena, deganawa,di,
segments.translation: I found some… I guess last Friday I found some Hickory Chicken. I brought them home and my wife cleaned them. I think it was last Sunday we ate them. I cut down a hickory tree by the house and where the stump is, they started growing there. [laughs] I took them off and then my youngest boy, he brought what he found. Also that Lion’s Mane, I find them sometimes. You can find them right now, too.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They know those things?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎠᏂᏧᏣ,? Oh, yeah! ᏕᏡ,Ꭼ’Ꮕ ᏍᏊ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏚᎾᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏗᎨᏲᏅ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏓᏬᎵ, ᏄᏍᏛ, Ꮧ’ᎤᏖᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, … Ꭺ-ᎪᏧᎾ,
segments.transliteration: anitsutsa,? Oh, yeah! detlu,gv’nv squu nigada, dunanv,ta, digeyonv nowu’nv, nigada, dawoli, nusdv, di’utesdi, gehv nowu’nv, … go-gotsuna,
segments.translation: The boys? Oh, yeah! The trees and everything, I’ve taught them to them. The mushrooms, which ones that are good to pick. Then Kochun.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You said that, do you like that?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Oh, yeah! It’s good to eat! Phew! How about you?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Huh uh! ᎠᏒᎦ’Ꮽ, ᏍᎩᎾ Ꭰ-Ꭰ-ᎠᎬᏂᏍᏗᎲ Ꮭ ᏯᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮧ,
segments.transliteration: Huh uh! asvga’wu, sgina a-a-agvnisdihv tla yagilvquo,di,
segments.translation: Uh uh! I like the way it smells, but I don’t like to eat it.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎤᏗᏞᎩ, ᎪᎢ, Ꭴ-Ꭴ-ᎤᏠᏱ Ꮎ Ꮎ watercress.
segments.transliteration: uditlegi, goi, u-u-utloyi na na watercress.
segments.translation: It’s good with some hot grease, just like Watercress.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: I like that Kochun that you’re talking about.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: It’s strong flavored/spicy.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I don’t like it, Kochun.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: It’s like watercress, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎥᎥ … Ꮎ’Ꮕ ᏐᎢ, Ꭴ-- Ꮎ … Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏚᏙᎥ ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, ᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᏧᏣ, ᎠᏴ’Ꮕ ᎠᏴ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᏅᏟ, Ꮵ’ᎡᎲ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎯᏲᎵᎦ, ᏱᎩ, ᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᏧᏣ, ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, ᏧᏙᎢᏓ, Ꭴ:ᏔᎾ, “ᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᏧᏣ,” ᎠᏃᏎᎮ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ)
segments.transliteration: vv … na’nv soi, u-- na … tla squu yawanv,ta, dudov ‘ahena, usdi atsutsa, ayv’nv ayv tsosdadanvtli, tsi’ehv tla yawanv,ta, hiyoliga, yigi, usdi atsutsa, ‘ahena, tsudoida, u:tana, “usdi atsutsa,” anosehe (uyetsi,sgv)
segments.translation: Yeah. Then there’s the other one, I don’t know what it’s called. Me and Usdi Atsutsa, my brother. I don’t know if you know him. Usdi Atsutsa – Clarence was his name. He was real big and they called him “Usdi Atsutsa.” [laughs]

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: I remember him.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎥᎥ Bell-Ꭲ ᏗᏢ, ᏍᏊ Ꮧ--… ᏍᎩᎾ ᏧᏪᏅᎲ ᏗᏢ, ᏬᏥᎶᏍᎬ Ꮎ bean Ꮎ vine ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎠᏛᏍᎬ, ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: vv Bell-i ditlv, squu di--… sgina tsuwenvhv ditlv, wotsilosgv na bean na vine yusdi, advsgv, tsigehv
segments.translation: Yeah, in Bell. We were going by his house, that Bean Vine, they call it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Uhyvhat(a).

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᏥᎨ-- Ꭴ-ᎤᏴᎭᏔ, ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᏂᏓᏥᏪᏏ, ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ … ᏙᏧᏖᏍᎬ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ, ᏍᏊ ᎤᎾᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎠᏂᏧᏣ, ᏍᎩᎾᎾ Ꭴ-- Ꮎ ᏕᏡ,Ꭼ ᏚᎾ,ᏙᎥ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏍᏊ ᎤᎾᏅ,Ꮤ
segments.transliteration: sgi’dv tsige-- u-uyvhata, sgi’dv nidatsiwesi, ‘ahena, tla yawanv,dv squu sginana … dotsutesgv, tsigehv sgina anitsutsa, squu unanv,ta, yusdi, gehv sgina ‘ahena, nigada, anitsutsa, sginana u-- na detlu,gv duna,dov nigada, squu unanv,ta
segments.translation: That’s what it was. Uhyvhata is what I’m going to say. But I don’t know. That’s what we used to pick, my boys know what it is. I try to teach them that, the trees and their names.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Do they like to eat stuff like that?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Oh, yeah, yeah! They sure do!

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎾᎾ ᏗᏣᏛᏏᏗᏒ Ꮎ ᏱᏗᏥᎵᏍᏆᏗ ᏱᏗᏥᏳᏆᏗ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏨᏥᏍᎪ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, … ᎠᎦ,ᏔᎮ Ꮎ … ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, Ꮎ--
segments.transliteration: nana ditsadvsidisv na yiditsilisquadi yiditsiyuquadi’le yigi, tsvtsisgo, tsigehv gohu,sdi, … aga,tahe na … gohu,sdi, na--
segments.translation: How about when you were growing up and you had an earache or a toothache? Did your mom know anything for that?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎢᏣᎩ,’Ꮫ ᏧᏙᎢᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ Ꭰ’ᎠᏴᎵᎨ well, Ꮭ Ꭰ’ᎠᏴᎵᎨ ᏥᎨᎲ ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, ᎤᏍᏗ-ᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᎨᏯ, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᎨᎲ ᎤᏔᎾ’Ꮽ ᎠᏴ, ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: na itsagi,’dv tsudoida, tsigehv a’ayvlige well, tla a’ayvlige tsigehv ‘ahena, usdi-usdi ageya, nigada, hena, agayvlige gehv utana’wu ayv, gehv
segments.translation: There was an elderly woman named Itsag(i). She wasn’t really an old woman, I was just little. When you’re little, everyone seems old or grown up.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Was her last name Bird?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎢᏣᎩ, Bird/Byrd ᎤᎾ Mama ᏙᎦ,ᏘᏂᏙᎲ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ’Ꮓ … ᎤᏬᏛ Ꮎ ᎪᏛ ᎦᎴᏍᎬ
segments.transliteration: vv itsagi, Bird/Byrd una Mama doga,tinidohv ganvdadisgo’no … uwodv na godv galesgv
segments.translation: Yeah, Itsag(i) Bird. Mama would take us to her, I remember. She had a fire and she would get some of it out.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: She was using fire?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎠᏥᎳ, Ꭼ,ᏗᎲ ᏧᏬᏰᏂ, *ᎠᎢ* Ꮒ,ᏕᎬᏁᎲ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, … ᎠᎹ,
segments.transliteration: atsila, gv,dihv tsuwoyeni, *ai* ni,degvnehv nowu’nv, … ama,
segments.translation: She was using it. She was moving her hands doing this [gestures] then she had water…

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: …you would blow on it.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: You--We would blow on it.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ,… ᏌᏭ ᎮᎾ, ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᎦᏅᏓᏗ’Ꮕ, ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩ ᏥᎾᏮᏁᎸ ᎠᎴ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏘᎩ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᏍᏊ ᎠᎾ,ᏗᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮩ-- Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏯᎾ,ᏓᏙᎵᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: gohu,sdi, hena, tsanv,ta,… sawu hena, yuwaga,da, ganvdadi’nv, squu sgi tsinawvnelv ale agi,stigi gohu,sdi, hena, squu ana,dihv tsigehv do-- tla yawanv,ta, yana,dadolisdi
segments.translation: You know, there was something… I remember one time they put something on my hair and then they’d say something. I don’t know if they were praying or what.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ’Ꭱ ᏣᎾ,ᏗᎲ yep, ᏙᎯᏳ’Ꮫ Ꮎ’Ꮕ, … ᏐᎢ’Ꮕ, ᏐᎢ, ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏗ, ᏍᏊ ᏬᎨᏓᏍᏗ ᎩᎶ ᏳᏓᏂᎳ, ᏥᎨᎲ … yeah, ᎣᎦᏛᏌ,’Ꮫ ᏍᎩ ᏃᎦᏛ--ᏃᏣᏛᏁᎲ ᏂᎯ ᎤᏠᏱ ᏍᏊ ᏂᎯ Ꭽ-- yeah. … Yeah, ᏙᎯᏳ’Ꮫ
segments.transliteration: vv gohu,sdi’e tsana,dihv yep, dohiyu’dv na’nv, … soi’nv, soi, udvhisdi, squu wogedasdi gilo yudanila, tsigehv … yeah, ogadvsa,’dv sgi nogadv--notsadvnehv nihi utloyi squu nihi ha-- yeah. … Yeah, dohiyu’dv
segments.translation: Yeah, they were saying something. Then there was an old man we would go see when somebody got sick. Yeah, we grew up the same way as you. Yeah. That’s right.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏍᎩ’Ꭱ ᏂᎦᏓ, … ᏍᎩ’Ꭱ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏂᏓ-ᏂᏓᏕᎳᎰᏍᎬᎾ’Ꮺ ᎦᎶᏐᎲᏍᎦ,
segments.transliteration: sgi’e nigada, … sgi’e nigada, nida-nidadelahosgvna’we galosohvsga,
segments.translation: All these old things we know, without realizing it, they are passing away.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Oh, yeah!

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Also the language we speak, y’know?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᏥᏓᏝᏃᎮᎠ, ᎦᏅᏓᏗ ᎾᏮᎨᏫ,Ꮢ ᎨᎲ… ᎤᎪᏓ, ᎦᏅ--
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv tsidatlanohea, ganvdadi nawvgewi,sv gehv… ugoda, ganv--
segments.translation: With us talking here I remember what I have forgotten… I remember a lot.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏍᎩ-ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᎢᎦ ᎤᎵ,ᏍᎨᏗ, ᎩᎶ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏙᎦ-ᏙᎦᏓᏝᏃᎮᏛ ᏱᎩ, ᏲᏮᏅ,ᏓᏓᎲᎦ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ,’ᎡᎦ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏱᏣᏃᎮᏝ, ᏱᏮᎪᏩ,Ꮨ’Ꮺ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏨᏥ ᏥᎨᏒ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏣᏁᎲ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎳ, … ᎤᎾ ᏫᏣ,ᏘᏃᎯᎰ … ᎭᏅ,ᏓᏗᏍᎪ’Ꭸ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏨᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎴ ᏣᎵᏏ, ᎩᎶ’Ꮽ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏣᏚᏥ, “ᎯᎢ ᏓᎦᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂ, ‘ᎸᏢ’Ᏼ” “ᎯᎢ ᏄᏍᏕᏍᏗ,” ᎠᏗᏍᎬ Ꮭ ᏯᏅ,ᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ,?
segments.transliteration: sgi-sgi’dv iga uli,sgedi, gilo atsalagiha doga-dogadatlanohedv yigi, yowvnv,dadahvga, atsalagi,’ega gohu,sdi, yitsanohetla, yiwvgowa,ti’we sgina tsvtsi tsigesv nowule tsanehv anigayvla, … una witsa,tinohiho … hanv,dadisgo’ge gohu,sdi, tsvtsi tsigehv ale tsalisi, gilo’wu, yusdi, tsadutsi, “hii dagali,stani, ‘lvtlv’yv” “hii nusdesdi,” adisgv tla yanv,dadisgo gohu,sdi,?
segments.translation: That’s how important it is to be able to talk to someone else all in Cherokee. You can remember a lot of old things. When you talk about something in Cherokee, you can see it, what it was. My mom and the other elders that used to be around, it takes you back then. Do you remember your mother, or grandmother, or your uncle saying, “This is what’s going to happen, this is how it’ll be.” Do you remember anything like that?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Not really.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ Stoney Stoney ᏥᎨᎲ Eagle ᎯᏲᎵᎦ,’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: ganvdadisgo Stoney Stoney tsigehv Eagle hiyoliga,’dv tsigehv
segments.translation: I remember Stoney. Stoney Eagle. You knew him, right?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Yeah, I know him.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: “ᎡᏙᏓ,-ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎹ, ᎦᏅᎪᎬ ᏙᏍᏓᏗᏔᏍᎬ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎤᏴᏟ--I mean, ᎤᏗᏞᎩ ᎠᎹ, ᎤᏴᏜ, ᏙᏍᏓᏗᏔᏍᎬ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏗᎬ ᏥᎨᎲ” ᏣᏗᎲ “’Boy, ‘ᏧᏣ, ‘ᎸᏢ’ᏴᎥ ᎠᎹ, ᏣᏩᏍᎨᏍᏗ,’ ᎠᏬᎮᎸ” ᏣᏗᎲ “’Hey, ᏯᎩᏩᏍᎬ, ᎠᎹ hey ᏂᎬ ᎮᎾ, ᎦᏁᎯ,’ ᎠᏪᎵᎲ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎠᏩᏔᎾ, ᏫᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾ,’Ꮓ ᎠᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᎠᎹ, ᎠᎩᏩᎯᏍᏗ … ᏕᎦᏈᏱ ᏏᏅᏓ,” ᏣᏗᎲ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎤᎾᏅ,Ꮦ ᎮᎾ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, … ᎤᎾᏅ,Ꮦ ᎮᎾ, ᏗᏓᏁᏟᏴᏏᏒ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ,
segments.transliteration: “edoda,-edoda, tsigehv ama, ganvgogv dosdaditasgv” tsadihv “uyvtli--I mean, uditlegi ama, uyvdla, dosdaditasgv” tsadihv “agi,sdigv tsigehv” tsadihv “’Boy, ‘tsutsa, ‘lvtlv’yvv ama, tsawasgesdi,’ awohelv” tsadihv “’Hey, yagiwasgv, ama hey nigv hena, ganehi,’ awelihv” tsadihv “awatana, winuli,stana,’no awalenvhv ama, agiwahisdi … degaquiyi sinvda,” tsadihv sgi yusdi, unanv,te hena, gohu,sdi, … unanv,te hena, didanetliyvsisv gohu,sdi,
segments.translation: “Me and Dad used to drink from the spring when it was hot outside. But we were drinking cold water,” he said. “I was just little,” he said. “Dad said, ‘Boy, someday you’re going to be buying water,’” he said. “Hey, why would I be buying water? When there’s water everywhere, I thought,” he said. “When I got older I started buying water and I’m paying for it every month,” he said. They knew that much. [the elders] They knew things were going to change.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Yep, ᏙᎯᏳ’Ꮫ … Boy ᎠᏴ,’Ꮫ ᎠᏮᎨᏫ,ᏍᎪ ᏗᏩᏛᏒ ᎾᏮᏛᏁᎲ … ᏯᏩᏚᎵ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎠᏩᏅ,ᏓᏗᏍᏗ ᎾᏩᏛᏁᎲ ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, ᎠᏮᎨᏫ,ᏍᎪ … ᎾᎮᎾ, Ꮎ … ᏌᎵ,’Ꮫ ᏣᏃᏎᎲ … Oak--Ꮎ’Ꮫ Sally Bull-Ꭲ ᏗᏢ, ᏥᏩᏂᏁᎸ … ᎤᎾ ᏱᏣᎷᏣ, Ꮎ Sally Bull … ᎧᎿᎷ--…ᏱᏣᎷᏣ,’Ꮓ ᎦᏚ ᏥᏩᏂᏁᎸ ᎢᎾ ᎧᎿᎷᏌ, ᏱᏣᎿᎷᏌ, ᎢᎾ caves Ꮒ,ᏕᎬᏅ ᎢᎾ ᏓᏂᏁᎸ ᎾᎥ … ᎠᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮧ, ᎨᎲ ᏩᏪᏓᏍᏗ … ᏚᏐᏴ’Ꮕ ᎢᎾᎾ … ᏔᎵ, caves Ꮒ,ᏕᎬᏅ … “’Ꮩ’Ꮕ, ᏥᏗᏣ,ᏐᏯ,?” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎢᎾ’Ꮫ ᏏᏆ, ᏕᏥᏴᏓ,” ᏣᏗᎲ … Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᏗᎪᏩ,Ꮨ ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, Ꮎ ᏓᏛᎯᏍᏗᎲ ᏏᏆ, … ᏄᏓᎭ Ꮭ ᏱᏓᎪᏩ,ᏘᎲ ᏣᏗᎲ ‘Ꮧ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏴᏭ ᏫᎦᎶᏍᎬ ᎾᎾ cave ᎢᎾ
segments.transliteration: Yep, dohiyu’dv … Boy ayv,’dv awvgewi,sgo diwadvsv nawvdvnehv … yawaduli nigada, awanv,dadisdi nawadvnehv ‘ahena, awvgewi,sgo … nahena, na … sali,’dv tsanosehv … Oak--na’dv Sally Bull-i ditlv, tsiwaninelv … una yitsalutsa, na Sally Bull … kahnalu--…yitsalutsa,’no gadu tsiwaninelv ina kahnalusa, yitsahnalusa, ina caves ni,degvnv ina daninelv nav … agilvquo,di, gehv wawedasdi … dusoyv’nv inana … tali, caves ni,degvnv … “’do’nv, tsiditsa,soya,?” tsadihv “ina’dv siqua, detsiyvda,” tsadihv … tla howa digowa,ti ‘ahena, na dadvhisdihv siqua, … nudaha tla yidagowa,tihv tsadihv ‘di yawanv,ta, yvwu wigalosgv nana cave ina
segments.translation: Yeah, they really did. Boy, I forget how I grew up, what I was doing. I wish I could remember it all what I did, but I forget. That one they call Sali they live in Sally Bull [Hollow]. When you get to Sally Bull, they live on a hilltop. When you climb up there, there’s caves up there, and they live next to them. I used to like to go there. There were fences around two caves. “Why do you have a fence?” I said. “That’s where I keep my hogs,” he said. He hardly saw them ‘cause they were in the cave. [laughter] “Sometimes I don’t see them at all,” he said. I don’t know how far back the cave went.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That’s where they went in?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: That’s where they went in at.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎪ,Ꮧ’Ꭱ ᎤᏂᎦ,ᏙᎲᏒ ᎨᎮ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎳ, ᏣᏁᎲᎢ ᏱᎩ, Ꮎ ᏗᎨᎩᏚᏓ, ᏗᎨᎩᎵᏏ, … ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎪ,Ꮧ *coughs* ᏥᎪ--ᏫᏥᎪᏩ,ᏘᎰ ᎡᏚᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᏱᎢᏢ ᏳᏬᏝ, ᎦᏅᏃᏩ, ᏱᎪᏍᎬ, … ᎡᎵᏭ ᏍᎩᎦᏚ’Ꮲ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮵ-ᏥᏯᏅᏓᏗ--boy ᎪᎯ, ᏥᎩ, ᏱᏩᏩᏓᏅ,ᏖᏝ, ᏓᏤᏝ,’ᎡᎧ ᏱᏥᏯᏛᏛᎮᏢᏅ ᎠᏬᎯᏳᏒ ᎨᎵ … ᎾᎮᎾ, ᏱᏕᎪᏪᎸᎦ,’ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᎵᏭ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎦᎵ,--ᎦᎵ,ᏆᏍᎪᎯ,’Ꮫ ᎤᎶᏒᏍᏗ, ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏱᏕᎪᏪᎸᎦ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏲᏁᎩ’Ꮕ, ᎬᏗ, “’Ꮩ’Ꮫ ᎡᎵ ᎤᏕᎶ,ᏆᎡ?” ᎩᎵ’Ꮕ, ᏥᎩ, ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, ᎠᏩ,ᏔᎾ, ᏂᎨᏐ ᎩᎳ, ᎠᏩᏟᏴᎦᏓᏁᎸ ‘Ꮩ ᎡᎵ ᎤᏕᎶ,ᏆᎥ
segments.transliteration: usquanigo,di’e uniga,dohvsv gehe anigayvla, tsanehvi yigi, na digegiduda, digegilisi, … usquanigo,di *coughs* tsigo--witsigowa,tiho eduda, tsigehv doyiitlv yuwotla, ganvnowa, yigosgv, … eliwu sgigadu’tlv yawadetiyvda, tsigehv tsi-tsiyanvdadi--boy gohi, tsigi, yiwawadanv,tetla, datsetla,’eka yitsiyadvdvhetlvnv awohiyusv geli … nahena, yidegowelvga,’hena, tsigehv eliwu udvhisdi tsigehv gali,--gali,quasgohi,’dv ulosvsdi, yudetiyvda, atsalagiha yidegowelvga, tsigehv yonegi’nv, gvdi, “’do’dv eli udelo,quae?” gili’nv, tsigi, gohi tsigi, awa,tana, nigeso gila, awatliyvgadanelv ‘do eli udelo,quav
segments.translation: They were smart, our grandfathers and grandmothers. It was interesting, I can still see my grandpa sitting on the porch with a pipe. I was about 15 years old, I remember--But I should’ve been asking him a lot of things. He could write. He was old, he was over 70 years old. He could write in both Cherokee and English. “How did he learn that?” Recently, today, now that I’m grown up, I’ve just realized how he learned it.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Me, if somebody…don’t teach you, you’re not going to learn it.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Ain’t it?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᎤᏍᏗᎧᏂ, ᏦᏍᏓᏓᎸ Ꮎ’Ꮕ, Ꭴ--ᎤᏍᏗᎧᏂ, ᎠᏧᏣ, ᎠᏩᏤᎵ ᎤᏅᏌ, ᏯᏃᏪᎸᎦ,
segments.transliteration: ayv, hena, usdikani, tsosdadalv na’nv, u--usdikani, atsutsa, awatseli unvsa, yanowelvga,
segments.translation: My youngest sister and my youngest son, they are the only ones who can write.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: In Cherokee?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏱᏓᏂᎪᎵᏱ’Ꮕ, … ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, Oak Ridge ᎮᎾ, ᏓᏩᏕᎶ,--ᎤᎾ ᏧᏂᎳᏫ,ᏍᏗ ᎡᏙᎲ Ꮎ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᎸ ᎤᎾᎢ’Ꮕ, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏓᏅ,ᏗᎰ Ꮟ … Ꮎ ᏣᎳᎩ, bible … ᎠᏅ,ᏗᎰ … Sunday School-Ꭲ’Ꮕ, ᏱᎩ, ᏃᏭ, ᏓᏁᏲᎲᏍᎪ Ꮟ ᎤᎾ ᏧᏂᎳᏫ,ᏍᏗ … ᎤᏂᎪᎵᏲᏰᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: vv yidanigoliyi’nv, … ayv, hena, Oak Ridge hena, dawadelo,--una tsunilawi,sdi edohv na tsosdadalv unai’nv, nigada, danv,diho si … na tsalagi, bible … anv,diho … Sunday School-i’nv, yigi, nowu, daneyohvsgo si una tsunilawi,sdi … unigoliyoyesdi
segments.translation: Mhm. And they can read it. My sister goes to church at Oak Ridge, they still use it all the time. [syllabary] They use the Cherokee Bible. And in Sunday School, they teach it to them to read, still.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: They’re doing good.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: We do the same at Belfonte Church.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Ꭳ Ꮎ ᏍᏊ? ᎣᏍᏓ’Ꭱ Salem’ᎮᎾ, ᏍᏊ Ꮟ ᏍᎩ ᎾᎾ,ᏛᏁᎰ
segments.transliteration: o na squu? osda’e Salem’hena, squu si sgi nana,dvneho
segments.translation: Oh, there, too? That’s good. They still do that at Salem, too.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏳᏓᎭ ᎠᏂ-…ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᏃᎵ,Ꭼ, ᏂᎨᎲᎾ, ᏯᏂᎷᎦ, ᏍᎩ’Ꮓ ᏱᏄᎾ,ᏛᏁᎳ, ᎡᏧᎳ, ᏗᎬᏁ,--ᏂᎬᏁᎰ ᎦᎵᏣᏙᎲᏍᎬ
segments.transliteration: yudaha ani-…tsalagi, anoli,gv, nigehvna, yaniluga, sgi’no yinuna,dvnela, etsula, digvne,--nigvneho galitsadohvsgv
segments.translation: Sometimes, people who don’t understand Cherokee will come. Then I’ll use both, English and Cherokee, when I preach.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎾᎮᎾ, Canaan ᎮᎾ, … ᏧᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᎠᎭᏂ, Cherokee Nation Canaan Duncan ᎯᏲᎵᎩ?
segments.transliteration: nahena, Canaan hena, … tsulvwi,sdanehv ahani, Cherokee Nation Canaan Duncan hiyoligi?
segments.translation: Canaan. He works at Cherokee Nation. Canaan Duncan. Do you know him?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: Ꮭ’Ᏺ ᏥᏲᎵᎩ, ᏱᎩ, ᏥᏯᏛᎦᏅ’Ꭱ ᏍᎩᏍ ᏤᏥ, ᎠᏧᏣ,?
segments.transliteration: tla’yo tsiyoligi, yigi, tsiyadvganv’e sgis tsetsi, atsutsa,?
segments.translation: I don’t really know him, but I’ve heard of him. Is that your son?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s my son.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: He was a council member.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᏥᎨᎲ ᎥᎥ ᏃᏭ … Ꮭ ᏍᏊ Ꮭ ᏱᎦᏛ--staff ᎨᎵ ᏃᏭ, Chief’s staff, he’s Chief’s staff Ꮭ ᏱᎨᏥᏯᏛᏛᎲᏍᎪ ᎾᎾᏛᏁᎲ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᏍᎩ’Ꮽ ᎮᎾ, ᎢᎦ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᎾᎾ Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᎤᏔᏂᏓ, ᎠᏧᏣ, ᎠᏩᏤᎵ ᎠᎭᏂ, Ꮎ Hastings ᏅᏬᏘ, ᏗᏓᏁᎯ, … He’s going about 10 years ᎾᏛᏁᎲ ᎤᎾ
segments.transliteration: tsigehv vv nowu … tla squu tla yigadv--staff geli nowu, Chief’s staff, he’s Chief’s staff tla yigetsiyadvdvhvsgo nanadvnehv diniyotli, sgi’wu hena, iga (uyetsi,sgv) nana na’nv, utanida, atsutsa, awatseli ahani, na Hastings nvwoti, didanehi, … He’s going about 10 years nadvnehv una
segments.translation: Yeah, he was. I’m not sure, now. I think he’s staff, Chief’s staff. I don’t really ask what my kids are doing. That’s it. [laughs] My oldest son, he works over at Hastings pharmacy. He’s going on about 10 years working there.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Do you have grandchildren?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎥᎥ yeah, ᏔᎵ, ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣ, ᏔᎵ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ, ᎡᏧᎳ, ᎠᏂᏧᏣ, ᎠᏧᏣ, ᎠᎨᏳᏣ, ᏚᏂᎧᎭ, ᏔᎵ’Ꮕ, ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣ, ᏧᎾ,ᏔᏂᏓ, Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᎠᏂᏧᏣ, ᎤᏔᏂᏓ,’Ꮫ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ, ᏐᏁᎳ, Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᏐᎢ, ᎠᎨᏳᏣ, ᏑᏓᎵ, … Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᎠᏧᏣ, ᏅᎩ, ᏐᎢ’Ꮕ, ᏦᎢ, … ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᏯᎩ,ᏑᎵ,ᎪᏣ, ᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏔᎵ’ᎮᎾ, Maryetta ᏓᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᎪ ᏔᎵ’Ꮕ, Zion-Ꭲ ᏯᎩ,ᏑᎵ,ᎪᏣ, Maryetta ᏫᎨᏙᎰ ᏕᏥᏯᏂᏍᎪ ᏔᎵ, … ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, Zion-Ꭲ ᏗᏢ, ᏬᏥᎶᏍᎪ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᏐᎢ, ᏕᏥᏯᏂᏍᎪ ᏃᏭ ᎣᏣᏂ’ᎢᏍᎪ ‘ᏓᏁᎸ ᎯᏍᎩ, ᎠᏰᏟ,’Ꮫ ᏑᏓᎵ,’ᎸᏢ ᎠᏁᏙᎰ’Ꮓ ᏧᎾ,--ᎠᏂᎷᎪ
segments.transliteration: vv yeah, tali, anigeyutsa, tali anitsutsa, etsula, anitsutsa, atsutsa, ageyutsa, dunikaha, tali’nv, anigeyutsa, tsuna,tanida, na’nv, anitsutsa, utanida,’dv ageyutsa, sonela, na’nv, soi, ageyutsa, sudali, … na’nv, atsutsa, nvgi, soi’nv, tsoi, … ayv, hena, yagi,suli,gotsa, dagilvwi,sdanehv tali’hena, Maryetta dana,delo,quasgo tali’nv, Zion-i yagi,suli,gotsa, Maryetta wigedoho detsiyanisgo tali, … nowu’nv, Zion-i ditlv, wotsilosgo na anisoi, detsiyanisgo nowu otsani’isgo ‘danelv hisgi, ayetli,’dv sudali,’lvtlv anedoho’no tsuna,--anilugo
segments.translation: Yes. Two grandgirls and two grandboys. Both of my boys have a boy and a girl. The girls are older. One is nine and the other is six. And then one boy is four and the other is three. When I get off work… Two of them go to school at Maryetta and the other two go to Zion. When I get off work, I go and get the two from Maryetta and then we go over to Zion and get the last two. Then we go home. They stay until about 5:30 – 6:00pm, then their parents come home.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: That’s good, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Yeah, it works out great.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Do they play ball? [Randy’s boys]

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎩᎳ, ᎠᎾᎴᏂᎠ, Ꮎ Ꭴ-- Ꮎ ᎤᏔᏂᏓ, ᏥᎩ, … Softball’Ꭱ ᏓᏁᎶᎲᏍᎪ Ꮎ fastpitch ᎤᎾ ᏛᎵ,Ꮟ ᏗᏢ, Ꮎ “traveling team” ᏣᏃᏎᎰ ᏓᏁᎶᎲᏍᎪ … right-field, center—Well, any field…ᎤᎾ ᏗᏢ, ᏩᏅᏁᎲ’Ꮽ … ᏫᎦᎶᏍᎪ ᎣᏍᏓ’ᎮᎾ, Ꭴ-ᎤᏍᏆᏞᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: gila, analenia, na u-- na utanida, tsigi, … Softball’e danelohvsgo na fastpitch una dvli,si ditlv, na “traveling team” tsanoseho danelohvsgo … right-field, center—Well, any field…una ditlv, wanvnehv’wu … wigalosgo osda’hena, u-usquatlesdi
segments.translation: They’re just now starting to play, the older ones. He plays fast-pitch softball in Tulsa with the “traveling team,” they call it. He plays right field, or center field, or any field. Whichever way they hit is where he plays, ‘cause he can catch the ball good.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎩᏂᏭᏗ, ᏥᏥᎪᎥ ᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎠ, Canaan Saturday night.
segments.transliteration: giniwudi, tsitsigov nawali,sdanea, Canaan Saturday night.
segments.translation: It seems like I saw Canaan at Kenwood last Saturday night.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Saturday ᏥᎨᎲ ᎥᎥ ᎥᎥ … ᎤᎸᏉ,Ꮧ, ᎤᎾ ᎤᏪᏓᏍᏗ ᎩᏂᏭᏗ, Canaan.
segments.transliteration: Saturday tsigehv vv vv … ulvquo,di, una uwedasdi giniwudi, Canaan.
segments.translation: Yeah, Saturday night. Canaan likes to go there, Kenwood.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: He likes what they’re building there.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: That’s what he said. “They were giving out Kanuchi.”

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah, that was me.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s what he said! “Charlie made it!”

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It was made with hominy.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Was it sweet, the hominy?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Hominy. Boy, ᎢᎦ ᎠᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮧ, hominy ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎢ ‘ᏓᏁᎸ Boy, ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᏐᎯ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, … 2 or 3 gallons ᏓᎩᎭ, ‘ᏓᏁᎸ garage-Ꭲ ᏗᏭᏖᏗ,
segments.transliteration: Hominy. Boy, iga agilvquo,di, hominy ayv, hena, ai ‘danelv Boy, ayv’dv sohi, tla yawanv,ta, … 2 or 3 gallons dagiha, ‘danelv garage-i diwutedi,
segments.translation: Boy, I like hominy. Over at the house, I don’t know…I’ve probably got about two or three gallons of walnuts that I picked in the garage.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Just here recently?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Yeah!

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Can you make Kanuchi?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Well, Canaan’Ꮫ ᎪᏢᏍᎪ ᎤᏅ,Ꮤ, … Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᎤᏬᏢᏗ ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, Ꮭ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎤᏛᏁᎴᏍᏗ, ᏚᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ, ᎠᎮ … ᏍᎩᎾ, Ꮒ,ᏥᏪᏎᎸ ᎢᎸᏍᎩ, ᏄᎲ ᎠᏓᏁᎸ ᏤᏙᎲ “Hey, ᎾᎮᎾ, ᏐᎯ, ᎣᏍᏓ,-ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏂᏨᏁ,Ꮧ,’Ꮫ” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ
segments.transliteration: Well, Canaan’dv gotlvsgo unv,ta, … na’e uwotlvdi ‘ahena, tla gohu,sdi, udvnelesdi, dulvwi,sdanehv, ahe … sgina, ni,tsiweselv ilvsgi, nuhv adanelv tsedohv “Hey, nahena, sohi, osda,-osda, nitsvne,di,’dv” tsiyohehv
segments.translation: Well, Canaan makes it. He knows how to make it. He hasn’t done anything, just working. I was telling him the other night, “Hey, you need to fix them walnuts.”

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: What do they call it? “Asdosdi?” – To grind

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Me, I pick out the goodies.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: All of them? You do all of them?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah, there’s hardly any of the walnut shell in the Kanuchi.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: You know that Jerry Bigfeather?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏧᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎯ, … Ꮭ’Ᏺ *ᎠᎭᏂ,* Ꮎ Cherokee Nation Environmental ᏧᏪᏅᎲ ᏥᏫ,ᎨᏙᎲ ᏕᏡ,Ꭼ ᎣᏍᏓ, Ꮒ,--Ꮒ,ᏕᏥᏴᏁᎸ Ꮎ … ᏧᏪᏅᎲ--ᏧᏪᏅᎲ ᎾᎥ … Ꮎ bucket truck ᎬᏗᎲ ᎣᏍᏓ, Ꮒ,ᏕᏥᏴᏁᎲ “Well…ᏩᏙ” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ “Hey! ᎧᏅᏥ ᏓᎩᎭ, ᎠᏭ, ᏐᎭᏫᏂ, ᏱᏕᏣᏚᎵᎮ” ᏣᏬᎮᎸ “ᎥᎥ ᏌᏭ’Ꮫ” – “ᏦᎢ,-ᏦᎢ,’Ꭸ ᏕᏣᏚᎵ?” – “Huh uh, ᏌᏭ’Ꮫ” Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏚᎵᎲ ᏂᎦ … ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, ᏌᏭ ᏣᎩᏁᎸ … New Year’s ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏂᏓ’ᎥᏁᎵ,
segments.transliteration: ahani, tsulvwi,sdanehi, … tla’yo *ahani,* na Cherokee Nation Environmental tsuwenvhv tsiwi,gedohv detlu,gv osda, ni,--ni,detsiyvnelv na … tsuwenvhv--tsuwenvhv nav … na bucket truck gvdihv osda, ni,detsiyvnehv “Well…wado” awohelv “Hey! kanvtsi dagiha, awu, sohawini, yidetsadulihe” tsawohelv “vv sawu’dv” – “tsoi,-tsoi,’ge detsaduli?” – “Huh uh, sawu’dv” tla yawadulihv niga … ‘ahena, sawu tsaginelv … New Year’s osda, nida’vneli,
segments.translation: He works here. Not really, here [gestures], Cherokee Nation, he works for the Environmental. I was at his house, fixing trees for him. I was using that bucket truck, fixing them. He said, “Well…thank you. I have some Kanuchi balls. Do you want some?” -- “Alright, I’ll take one,” I said. “Do you want three of them?” – “Uh uh, just one.” I didn’t want one, but he gave it to me anyway. I’m going to fix it up on New Year’s.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Ooh!

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: You’re going to cook it. [brew]

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: What do they call “Hominy” in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: “ᏓᎵᏭ” … Huh uh! Huh uh! Rice-Ꮫ ᏥᎩ, “ᏓᎵᏭ”
segments.transliteration: “daliwu” … Huh uh! Huh uh! Rice-dv tsigi, “daliwu”
segments.translation: “Daliwu”… Uh uh! That’s rice.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Rice.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: [Groans] What do they call it?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: I forget things real quick.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Is it not…?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Me, all I know is “Ground Corn” – Selu Asdod(i).

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Ꮟ’Ꭱ ᏐᎢ, ᏐᎢ, ᎾᏂᏪᏍᎪ ᏙᎲ? ᎨᎵ ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᎢᎦ ᏴᏫ, ᏲᏛ’Ꭵ’Ꭰ-[ᏲᏛᎬᎦ,] ᏍᎩ ᏂᎦᏪᏍᎬ
segments.transliteration: si’e soi, soi, naniwesgo dohv? geli ‘ahena, tla sgi iga yvwi, yodv’v’a-[yodvgvga,] sgi nigawesgv
segments.translation: There’s something else they call it, ain’t it? But you don’t hear people saying it.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏝᏍᎪ, “ᏎᎷ ᎦᏁᎦᎸᏗ,” ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ,’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ,? ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ’Ᏺ ᏙᎲ? ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᏱᏄᏪᏌ, ᎩᎶ ᏲᎵ,Ꭶ, ᎮᎾ, ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: tlasgo, “selu ganegalvdi,” gohu,sdi,’le yigi, sgi yusdi,? sgi’dv squu’yo dohv? sgi hena, yinuwesa, gilo yoli,ga, hena, dohv?
segments.translation: But also, there’s “selu ganegalvd(i)” – peeled corn. If somebody says that, you know what they’re talking about.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Yeah, ᏃᏭ’Ꮫ Ꮎ pot-Ꭲ ᏣᏂᏢᏍᎬ, ᏍᎩᎾᎾ … ‘Ꮩ ᏍᎩ ᏥᎩ,? Ashes! ᎥᏍᎩᎾ ᎪᏢᏔᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏖᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: Yeah, nowu’dv na pot-i tsanitlvsgv, sginana … ‘do sgi tsigi,? Ashes! vsgina gotlvtanv sgina utedi, tsigehv
segments.translation: And then the pot that they put it in. They make it with the ashes, that’s when it’s really good.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎤᏍᏗᎧᏂ, ᎠᎩᎵᏏ, ᎠᏧᏣ, ᏕᏥᏲᎥ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎬᏗ, ᏃᏱ
segments.transliteration: na usdikani, agilisi, atsutsa, detsiyov tsalagi, gvdi, noyi
segments.translation: I named my youngest grandson Noyi.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What was it?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Noyi.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Noyi.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Do you know what that is?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Sand.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: That’s right.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Ain’t it?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᎢᎦᏓ, Ꮭ ᏳᎾᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏍᏊ
segments.transliteration: sgi’dv igada, tla yunanv,ta, yusdi, gehv na squu
segments.translation: Some people don’t know what it is. And also…

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: What about Nots(i)? – Pine, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎥᎥ … ᏓᎶᏂᎨ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᎤᏍᏘᎬ ᎤᏍᏗᎧᏂ,
segments.transliteration: vv … dalonige yusdi, hena, ustigv usdikani,
segments.translation: Yeah. … He has blonde hair, the youngest one.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Oh!

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: That’s why I named him Noyi.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Does Canaan have one to use?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᎠᏮᏌ, ᎠᏬᏢᏗ ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, Ꮎ ᏛᎩᏩᏏ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, bowl, to cut out. ᏍᏓᏱ ᎮᎾ, ᏂᎬᏁ,Ꮧ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: vv ayv’dv awvsa, awotlvdi ‘ahena, na dvgiwasi, gohu,sdi, bowl, to cut out. sdayi hena, nigvne,di dohv?
segments.translation: Yeah. I want to make it myself. I’m going to buy a bowl to cut out. It’s hard to do that, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: It’s work.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: It’s work.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: It’s strange why they charge $30 dollars for a Kanuchi ball.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ--ᎠᏴ’ᏛᏲ Ꮭ ᏲᏥᏂ,ᏚᎦ, Ꮭ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏌᎷᏱ ᎠᏭᏖᏗ, … ᏲᏥᏂ,ᏚᎦ,
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv--ayv’dvyo tla yotsini,duga, tla gohu,sdi, saluyi awutedi, … yotsini,duga,
segments.translation: Me, I’m not going to sell anything that I picked in the woods. I don’t sell it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏴ, ᎪᏢᏍᎪ ᏍᏊ … ᏳᏓᎭᏭ ᏴᏛᎾ, ᏐᎯ, ᎠᏓᏱ “ᏙᏘᎩᏏᏍᎪ,”-Ꭱ ᏱᎬᏬᏌ, … ᏱᏫ,ᏕᏥᎩ, ᎪᏢᏍᎪ ᎦᏥᏁᎰᎢ’Ꮕ,
segments.transliteration: ayv, hena, ayv, gotlvsgo squu … yudahawu yvdvna, sohi, adayi “dotigisisgo,”-e yigvwosa, … yiwi,detsigi, gotlvsgo gatsinehoi’nv,
segments.translation: I make it, too. I get calls all the time, telling me to come get some walnuts. I’ll go get them, then I’ll make it and give it to the people.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᏝᏍᎪ, ᏐᎢ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, Ꮸ,ᏔᏅ ᏱᎩ, ᎧᏅᏥ, Ꮎ pecan … ᏱᎩ? ᏎᏗ,’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ,?
segments.transliteration: tlasgo, soi, gohu,sdi, tsv,tanv yigi, kanvtsi, na pecan … yigi? sedi,’le yigi,?
segments.translation: You haven’t used something different for Kanuchi? Like, pecans? Or walnuts?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I want to try it.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: It might be good, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Well, they say it’s too rich ᏣᎾ,Ꮧ … ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᎥᎩᏃᏎᎸ ᎤᎪᏗ ᎢᎦ ᏱᏣᎦ, … ᏲᏍᏉᎵ,ᏗᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎾ,ᏗᎲ … Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏙᏳ, ᏱᎩ,
segments.transliteration: Well, they say it’s too rich tsana,di … ayv, hena, vginoselv ugodi iga yitsaga, … yosquoli,disdi, hena, ana,dihv … tla yawanv,ta, doyu, yigi,
segments.translation: Well, they say it’s too rich. I’ve also been told that if you eat too much of it, you’ll get diarrhea. I don’t know if it’s true.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎤᏠᏱ’Ꮕ, ᏍᏊ ᏏᏆ ᎤᏴᏓ, ᏙᎲ ᏲᏍᏉᎵ,ᏗᏍᏗ ᎮᎾ, ᏍᏊ
segments.transliteration: utloyi’nv, squu siqua uyvda, dohv yosquoli,disdi hena, squu
segments.translation: It’s the same with hog meat. If you eat too much, you’ll have diarrhea.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It’d be even more!

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: It’d be even more! Ain’t it?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎾᎾ ᎭᏅ,ᏓᏗᏍᎪ, Ꮎ … ᎤᏂᎿᏑᎩ,? ᎭᏅ,ᏓᏗᏍᎪ,? Gah, ᏍᎩ’ᎡᏲ! (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ)
segments.transliteration: nana hanv,dadisgo, na … unihnasugi,? hanv,dadisgo,? Gah, sgi’eyo! (uyetsi,sgv)
segments.translation: Do you remember possum grapes? You remember? Gah, those, too! [laughs]

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Yeah, those too! Ain’t it? Yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: They’re “Possum Grapes” in English. [laughs]

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎠᏴ,’Ꮕ, Ꭰ’ᎢᎭ, ‘ᏓᏁᎸ ᏃᏭ ᏥᎩ, ᎠᏬ-ᎠᏬᏢᏅ Ꮎ jelly…
segments.transliteration: ayv,’nv, a’iha, ‘danelv nowu tsigi, awo-awotlvnv na jelly…
segments.translation: I have some jelly at the house that I made…

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Possum grapes?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: …this year. Yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: They’re still around, huh?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Ꭳ! This year-Ꮫ’Ᏺ Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ, ᏣᏁᎲ Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᏍᏊ Ꮎ … grapes-Ꭲ’Ꮕ, ᏍᏊ wild grapes
segments.transliteration: o! This year-dv’yo tsi,quisdi, tsanehv na’nv, squu na … grapes-i’nv, squu wild grapes
segments.translation: Yeah, this year, there’s been a lot. And also, grapes, wild grapes.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You found some wild grapes?!

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Ooh, me too!

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: I’d say that’s surprising.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎾᎯᏳ’Ꮫ ᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ y’know ᏂᎬ ᎮᎾ, ᎦᎵᏟᏙᎰ ᏌᎷᏱ’Ꮕ, ᏕᎦᏅᏅ … ᏂᏥᎪᏩ,ᏘᎰ’Ꮫ I’ve got those feed sack ᎧᎵ Ꮣ’ᎢᎭ, … ᏓᎩᎾᏩ,ᏛᎲ Ꮎ wild grapes … Ꮟ ᎤᎾᏛ ᎤᎾ
segments.transliteration: nahiyu’dv dagilvwi,sdanehv y’know nigv hena, galitlidoho saluyi’nv, deganvnv … nitsigowa,tiho’dv I’ve got those feed sack kali da’iha, … daginawa,dvhv na wild grapes … si unadv una
segments.translation: But me working, I go all over the place, the roads and the woods. I see them. I’ve got a feed sack full that I found, wild grapes. There was still some hanging on the bush.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏍᏊ’Ꮫ Ꮎ ᏣᎨᏫᏍᏗ ᏂᎨᎲᎾ, ᎤᎾ’Ꭱ ᎤᎾᏛ
segments.transliteration: squu’dv na tsagewisdi nigehvna, una’e unadv
segments.translation: I guess you weren’t going to forget where they were hanging.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎥᎥ yeah Ꮎ’Ꮕ, possum grapes ᏂᎬ’Ꮫ
segments.transliteration: vv yeah na’nv, possum grapes nigv’dv
segments.translation: Yeah. And there’s possum grapes all over.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Huh!

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, ᎮᎾ, ᎪᏢᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᎾ, jelly … ᏍᎩ’Ꭱ ᏥᏓᎩᎾᏩ,ᏛᎲ Ꮎ wild grapes … half pint’ᏛᎮ ᏱᏕᎪᏌ, *ᎯᎢ*’Ꮫ ᏱᏗᎩᏓ, ᏅᎩ--ᎯᎩ,ᏍᎪᎯ, ᏣᏁᎳ, ᎢᎦ Ꮷ--ᏥᏚᏬᏢᏅ wild grapes
segments.transliteration: ayv, hena, agi,sdayvhvsgi, hena, gotlvsgo sgina, jelly … sgi’e tsidaginawa,dvhv na wild grapes … half pint’dvhe yidegosa, *hii*’dv yidigida, nvgi--higi,sgohi, tsanela, iga tsu--tsiduwotlvnv wild grapes
segments.translation: My wife makes jelly. That’s why I found those wild grapes. I guess you can say they’re half-pint jars. She fixed 58 of them.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᏔᎵᏁᎢ,’Ꮫ Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ, ᏕᏥᎾᏩ,ᏛᎲ ᏱᏕᎬᏃᎯᏏ, ᎨᎮᏍᏗ, Charlie
segments.transliteration: talinei,’dv tsi,quisdi, detsinawa,dvhv yidegvnohisi, gehesdi, Charlie
segments.translation: When I find some again, I will bring them to you, Charlie.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah, she can make it.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Yeah, ᎠᏴ,’Ꮫ ᎠᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮧ, ᎮᎾ, ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ,
segments.transliteration: Yeah, ayv,’dv agilvquo,di, hena, sgi yusdi,
segments.translation: Yeah, I really like that kind.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᏍᏊ elderberry. ᏂᎪᎯ,Ꮈ ᏱᎪᏢᎾ, ᏍᎩᎾ … ᏍᎩ’Ᏺ ᏴᏫ, ᎤᎾᏚᎵᎰ … ᏳᏬᏢᎾ, ᎤᏂᏩᎯᏍᏗ ᎤᎾᏚᎵᎰ Ꮒ,ᏗᎦᎵ,ᏍᏙᏗ ᏅᏬᏘ, ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎾ,ᏗᎰ
segments.transliteration: na’nv, squu elderberry. nigohi,lv yigotlvna, sgina … sgi’yo yvwi, unaduliho … yuwotlvna, uniwahisdi unaduliho ni,digali,sdodi nvwoti, hena, ana,diho
segments.translation: And also elderberry. She also makes that kind all the time. People are always wanting it. When she makes it, they want to buy it. Because they say it’s medicine.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: It’s good medicine, elderberry.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Don’t they call it “Kog(a)sad(i)” -- elderberry?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Kog(a)sad(i).

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: I forget the names of these berries.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏣᏗ Ꮎ ᎠᎭ,Ꮒ, ᎮᎾ, ᎩᎳ, ᏱᎩᏬᏂᏌ,--
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv squu sgina tsadi na aha,ni, hena, gila, yigiwonisa,--
segments.translation: Me too! Like you were saying, it’s not until we speak about it--

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: --that’s when I’ll remember.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Yeah!

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: And then, too, the Sassafras trees.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Kan(a)sdatl(i).

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Kan(a)sdatl(i) yeah!

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Ain’t it? I think that’s what it was, Kan(a)sdatl(i).

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎨᎵ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ Ꮎ … Ꮎ bark, Ꮭ’Ᏺ ᏙᏳ, bark Ꮎ boil Ꮎ--ᏥᏂ,ᏕᎬᏁᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ Mama Ꮎ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, Ᏺ’ᎢᎦᎵ,Ꮜ, … ᎭᏫᏂ, ᏱᎩ, ᏍᎩ’Ᏺ … ᏅᏬᏘ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏥᏂ,ᏕᏁᎲ ᏍᏊ
segments.transliteration: geli sginana na … na bark, tla’yo doyu, bark na boil na--tsini,degvnehv tsigehv Mama na gohu,sdi, yo’igali,sa, … hawini, yigi, sgi’yo … nvwoti, osda, tsini,denehv squu
segments.translation: Yeah, I think that one, was it tree bark? Mama used to boil it. When we cut it out real deep, she made medicine with it.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: That’s right, that’s right. Really.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: … Ꭲ-ᎢᏗᏣᎳᎩ, Ꮵ-ᏥᎪᎯᏳ ᏴᏓᎾ, ᏥᎩ, ‘Ꮵ,ᎩᎵ, ᏥᏓᏗᎰ ᎦᎾ,ᏰᎩ, ᏱᎩ, Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, Ꮳ-ᏣᎪᎲ ᏱᎩ,?
segments.transliteration: … i-iditsalagi, tsi-tsigohiyu yvdana, tsigi, ‘tsi,gili, tsidadiho gana,yegi, yigi, tla sgi yusdi, tsa-tsagohv yigi,?
segments.translation: I guess you could say that us Cherokees believe in Tsigil(i) – monsters. You haven’t seen anything like that?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Huh uh. ᎭᏗ--‘Ꮧ ᏱᎪᎯᏳᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ‘Ꮵ,ᎩᎵ, ᎠᏴ
segments.transliteration: Huh uh. hadi--‘di yigohiyusgo sginana ‘tsi,gili, ayv
segments.translation: Uh uh. I don’t believe in that, tsigil(i).

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: No? No?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᏍᏊ Ꮎ ᏙᎦᏛᏒ Ꮎ “ᏕᎯᏴᎯ!” ᏣᏗᎰ Mama “Ꮎ ᏧᏂ,ᏍᏗ ᎠᏂᏴᏫ,’Ꭱ ᎠᏁᏙᎯ, Ꮣ-ᏓᏰᏣ,ᏘᏁᏏ, ᎮᎾ, ᏂᏗᏥᏴᏢᎾ, ᏱᎩ,” ᏣᏗᎲ ᎣᎩᏍᎦᎮᏗ,’Ꮫ Ꮵ’ᎡᎲ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ … ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, ᏍᏊ ᎮᎾ, Ꭼ,ᏗᎲ ᎾᎥ’Ꮽ, Ꭳ’ᎡᏓᏍᏗ, ᏃᏥᎶᏒᎾ, ᎨᎲ … ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᎠᏂᏃᎮᎲ ᏍᏊ ᏧᏂ,ᏍᏗ ᎠᏂᏴᏫ, … ᏧᏂ,--ᎤᏂ,ᏘᏁᏒ ᏌᏭ … ᏧᏁᏅᎲ Ꮞ’ᎠᏨ ᎤᏂᏩᏛᎲ ᏣᏗᎲ y’know
segments.transliteration: na’nv, squu na dogadvsv na “dehiyvhi!” tsadiho Mama “na tsuni,sdi aniyvwi,’e anedohi, da-dayetsa,tinesi, hena, niditsiyvtlvna, yigi,” tsadihv ogisgahedi,’dv tsi’ehv nigohilv … ‘ahena, squu hena, gv,dihv nav’wu, o’edasdi, notsilosvna, gehv … nowu’nv, aninohehv squu tsuni,sdi aniyvwi, … tsuni,--uni,tinesv sawu … tsunenvhv se’atsv uniwadvhv tsadihv y’know
segments.translation: When we were growing up, Mama used to say, “Come in! There’s little people around, they’re going to take you away if you don’t come in!” We were afraid all the time. That was just what she was using for us to stay close by. They were talking about little people taking them to their home. They barely found their way back home.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎳ, ᏙᎲ? … ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎾᏂᏪᏢᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏣᏗ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏴ, … Ꮭ ᏍᏊ--Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮨ’Ꮕ, … ᏯᏂ-ᏯᏂ-ᏯᏂᏍᎦᏍᏗ’Ꮽ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ)
segments.transliteration: tsi,quisdi, hena, anigayvla, dohv? … sgi yusdi, naniwetlvsgv sgina, tsadi squu ayv, … tla squu--tla yawanv,ti’nv, … yani-yani-yanisgasdi’wu, tla yawanv,ta, (uyetsi,sgv)
segments.translation: There are a lot of elders who would say things like that to us too, like you’re saying. I don’t know if they were afraid too. [laughs]

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᎨᎵ ᏍᎩ’Ꮽ ᎠᎭ,Ꮒ, ᏃᏭ, ᏙᎦᏛᏐᎾ, ᏃᏭ, ᏍᎩ’ᎡᏲ ᎣᎩᏍᎦᏍᏗᎲ Mama ᎾᎥ’Ꮽ Ꭳ’ᎡᏓᏍᏗ, ᏒᎯᏰ--ᏒᏃᏱ ᏱᎩ, ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, … ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ,
segments.transliteration: sgi’dv geli sgi’wu aha,ni, nowu, dogadvsona, nowu, sgi’eyo ogisgasdihv Mama nav’wu o’edasdi, svhiye--svnoyi yigi, ‘ahena, … ‘ahena, tla yawanv,ta,
segments.translation: That’s what I think. Now that we’re grown, I think, “Boy, Mama was scaring us, so we’d stay close by at nighttime.” But I don’t know.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎩᎶ Ꮎ ᏤᎩᎵᏃᎮᏛ,(1:09:18) ᏥᎧᏃᎲᎳ, ᏙᎲ? ᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.transliteration: gilo na tsegilinohedv, tsikanohvla, dohv? sdi sgina
segments.translation: We talked to somebody who talked about something like that. [little people]

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: He talked about something peculiar.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎩᎶ Ꭴ-Ꭴ-ᎤᏂ,ᏘᏅᏒ Ꮎ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎧᏃᎮᏍᎨ ᏣᏗ, … “ᎦᏍᎩᎶ ᏚᏂᏍᎩᎸ ᎤᏂᎦ,ᏑᏘ,” ᎤᎾ,ᏛᏅ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ,
segments.transliteration: gilo u-u-uni,tinvsv na sgina, kanohesge tsadi, … “gasgilo dunisgilv uniga,suti,” una,dvnv sgi yusdi,
segments.translation: He said that the little people had taken somebody. “They told him to sit down in the chair and it was a rattlesnake!” they said.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: I’ve heard that before, too.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: He was talking about that.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: But me..

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You don’t believe that?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Huh uh. ᎭᏗ ᏝᏗ ‘Ꮵ,ᎩᎵ, ᏍᏊ Ꮭ
segments.transliteration: Huh uh. hadi tladi ‘tsi,gili, squu tla
segments.translation: Uh uh. Also, tsigil(i) – monsters, too.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about Bigfoot?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Uh uh! Not that either!
[laughter]

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎠᏴ,-ᎠᏴ, ᏍᎩ’Ᏼ ᎡᎵᏭ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎤᎪᎮ ᎩᎶ ‘ᎸᏢ’Ᏼ ᏥᎨᎲ … ᏍᎩ’Ꮽ ᏃᏭ, ᎤᏓᎴᏅᎮ ᎨᎵᏍᎪ ᎧᏱᏉᎬ’Ꮽ, ᎨᎵᏍᎪ ᎠᏴ, ᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᏯᏬᎯᏳ ᎡᎲ … ᏱᎨᎵ’ᏛᏭ ᏫᎦᎢᏒ’Ꮫ ᏙᏛᏂ,ᏗᏫ,Ꮟ, (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ)
segments.transliteration: ayv,-ayv, sgi’yv eliwu, gohu,sdi, ugohe gilo ‘lvtlv’yv tsigehv … sgi’wu nowu, udalenvhe gelisgo kayiquogv’wu, gelisgo ayv, gehv tla sgi yawohiyu ehv … yigeli’dvwu wigaisv’dv dodvni,diwi,si, (uyetsi,sgv)
segments.translation: Me, I think somebody just saw something way back and that’s when it started. People kept talking about ghosts and monsters. That’s what I think, I don’t believe it exists, but probably I’ll be walking, and one’s going to run across in front of me! [laughs]

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Y’know, ᎾᎮᎾ, Saturday—Saturday evening’Ꮫ ‘ᎡᎵ Ꮎ Osiyo-that-Tv ᎠᏩᎦ,ᏙᏍᏛ, … Thomas Belt ᎯᏲᎵᎩᏍᎪ,?
segments.transliteration: Y’know, nahena, Saturday—Saturday evening’dv ‘eli na Osiyo-that-Tv awaga,dosdv, … Thomas Belt hiyoligisgo,?
segments.translation: You know, last Saturday evening I was watching OsiyoTv. Do you know Thomas Belt?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah, yeah.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: North Carolina ᏗᏢ, ᏪᎮ ᏃᏭ, Ꮎ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, Ꭴ--ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏱᏂ,ᏓᏥᏪᏏ, ᏚᏙᎥ ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᎨᎵ ᏥᏂ,ᎦᏪᏍᎬ “ᏧᎾ ᏧᎳᏍᎩ,” … ᎯᏯᏛᎦᏅᏍᎪ, ᏍᎩᎾᎾ Ꮎ ᏧᎾ Rock? ᏧᎾ ᏧᎳᏍᎩ, ᏍᎩ ᎨᎵᏍᎬ ᏤᏮ North Carolina ᏗᏢ, Ꮎ … ᎢᏂ, ᏱᎦᏘ, … ᎠᏴᏫᏯ ᏤᎲ ᎤᎾ North Carolina ᏗᏢ, “giant” ᏣᏃᏎᎲ … ᎡᏙᎵᏙᎲ, ᏂᎬ ᎨᎲ ᏌᎷᏱ ᏣᎾ,ᏗᎲ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ “ᎤᎾ ᎦᏚᎢ, ᎡᏡ,Ꭼ ᎤᎩᎸ” ᏣᏗᎲ … ᎩᎶ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, Ꮒ,ᏕᎬᏁᎲ ᎠᏕᎳᎰᏍᎬ ᏃᏭ ᏚᎵ,ᏔᏗᏅᏒ ᎡᏡ,Ꭼ ᎤᎩᎸ “Ꭱ:ᎳᏗ, ᏧᎶᏒ” ᏣᏗᎲ ᎤᏔᎾ, rock ᎨᎲ land ᎤᎾ land ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᏍᎩ’Ꮓ ᏫᏚᎦ,ᏎᏍᏔᏅ ᏍᎩ’Ꮓ ᎤᎷᏨ ᎤᎾ Ꮎ ᏅᏱ ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᏱᏮᎪᏩᏔ, ᏃᏭ, ᎤᎾ North Carolina Ꮎ ᏅᏱ
segments.transliteration: North Carolina ditlv, wehe nowu, na tla yawanv,ta, u--osda, yini,datsiwesi, dudov sgi hena, geli tsini,gawesgv “tsuna tsulasgi,” … hiyadvganvsgo, sginana na tsuna Rock? tsuna tsulasgi, sgi gelisgv tsewv North Carolina ditlv, na … ini, yigati, … ayvwiya tsehv una North Carolina ditlv, “giant” tsanosehv … edolidohv, nigv gehv saluyi tsana,dihv sginana “una gadui, etlu,gv ugilv” tsadihv … gilo diniyotli, gohu,sdi, ni,degvnehv adelahosgv nowu duli,tadinvsv etlu,gv ugilv “e:ladi, tsulosv” tsadihv utana, rock gehv land una land nuli,stanv sgi’no widuga,sestanv sgi’no ulutsv una na nvyi sgi hena, yiwvgowata, nowu, una North Carolina na nvyi
segments.translation: He lives in North Carolina now. He said, and I don’t know if I’m going to say it right, but this is what he said, its name is “Tsuna Tsulasg(i).” Have you ever heard that? Tsuna Rock. Tsuna Tsulasg(i). It lives in North Carolina. It’s tall and an Indian living in North Carolina. And everybody said it was a giant. He roamed around over there in the woods. “He was on top of a tree,” he said. He [the giant] noticed somebody was doing something to the kids. He jumped out of the tree and he fell way down. He landed on a big rock. He watched. Then he came up to the rock. And you can still see that rock today in North Carolina.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: He landed on that rock?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᏫᏚᏥᏢ ᎤᎾ ᎤᏬ--ᎤᏬᏰᏂ, ᎤᎾ Ꮟ print ᏂᎬᎿ, ᎤᎾ ᏍᎩ’Ꮓ maps ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎤᏬᏢᏅ ᎤᎾᎾ ᏅᏱ
segments.transliteration: widutsitlv una uwo--uwoyeni, una si print nigvhna, una sgi’no maps gohu,sdi, uwotlvnv unana nvyi
segments.translation: Yeah, he landed on that rock. You can still see his handprint there. And he made a map on the rock.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: … Y’know, Ꮭ’Ᏺ…ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎠᎩᎪᎲ Ꮎ ᏅᏱ Ꮭ ᏯᎩᎪᏩ,ᏘᎲ--ᏱᏥᎪᏩ,ᏘᎲ Ꮎ ᎤᏬᏰᏂ, print ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ … ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᏧᏂᏃᎮᏢ ᏱᎪᏩ,Ꮤ, ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: … Y’know, tla’yo…ilvhiyu tsanv,ta, agigohv na nvyi tla yagigowa,tihv--yitsigowa,tihv na uwoyeni, print nuli,stanv … nowu’nv, tsuninohetlv yigowa,ta, tsigehv
segments.translation: Y’know, I had never seen that rock, and I wasn’t seeing his handprint, but when they talked about it, you could see it.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Maybe that is the reason that they are talking about Bigfoot nowadays.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᎠᏴ, Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ ᏱᎩ, ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, ᏱᏮᎪᏩᏔ, Ꮎ ᏅᏱ ᎥᎾ tour ᎤᎾ ᏱᏪᏙᎯ, North Carolina bridge-ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎪᏢᎢ, ᏱᏙᎬ, Ꭴ:ᏔᎾ ᏅᏯ, ᎠᎭ, ᎤᎾ
segments.transliteration: ayv, tla ilvhiyu aqua,dvganv yigi, ‘ahena, yiwvgowata, na nvyi vna tour una yiwedohi, North Carolina bridge-yusdi, gotlvi, yidogv, u:tana nvya, aha, una
segments.translation: I hadn’t heard of it. But if you go on the tour, you can see it in North Carolina. There’s a little bridge, and you stand there and see that big rock.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: There are people at Belfonte that really believe in that. [laughs]

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꮫ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᏍᏊ ᏥᏧᏣ’Ꮽ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᎾ,ᎳᏍᎦᎵᏍᎬ Ꮶ’ᎢᎦᏴᎵᎨ … ᎠᏭ, ᏧᎾ,ᏓᏂᏐᏗ ᎦᏓ, ᏥᏩᏂᎩᏍᎬ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: na’dv ganvdadisgo squu tsitsutsa’wu tsigehv na ana,lasgalisgv tso’igayvlige … awu, tsuna,danisodi gada, tsiwanigisgv tsigehv
segments.translation: I remember when I was just a boy, our parents were playing ball. They went and got dirt from the cemetery.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah! [laughs]

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: ᏣᏂᎷᎬ base-Ꭲ’Ꮫ Ꮎ ᎦᏓ ᎠᏂᎲᏍᎬ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏣᏅ,Ꮫ ᎤᏃᎮᏍᎬ? ᏣᏅ,ᏘᏍᎪ, ᏍᏊ ᏂᎯᎾ?
segments.transliteration: tsanilugv base-i’dv na gada anihvsgv tsigehv tsanv,dv unohesgv? tsanv,tisgo, squu nihina?
segments.translation: They’d come and put the dirt on the bases. [To Charlie] You know what that means? [To Mike] Do you know, too?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: I haven’t heard of it.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Yeah, ᎾᎾ ᏧᎾ,ᏓᏂᏐᏗ ᎦᏓ, ᏱᏫ,ᏣᎩᏌ, Ꮭ ᎩᎶ … ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏴᏮᎦ, Ꮎ ᏦᎳ ᎠᏅ,ᏗᎲ
segments.transliteration: Yeah, nana tsuna,danisodi gada, yiwi,tsagisa, tla gilo … gohu,sdi, yvwvga, na tsola anv,dihv
segments.translation: Yeah, if you get the dirt from the cemetery, nobody can do anything to you, by using tobacco.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They said it would break it up. [medicine]

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: “ᏯᏲᏍᏓ, -- ᎦᏙ ᏯᏲᏍᏓ, ᎩᎶ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎾᏛᏁᎠ,” … yeah, ᏯᏂᎲᏍᎬ, ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: “yayosda, -- gado yayosda, gilo sgi yinadvnea,” … yeah, yanihvsgv, tsigehv
segments.translation: “The dirt will break it, if somebody is doing that [using tobacco],” [they said.] Yeah, they were putting that on there.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎢᎦᏗ’Ꮕ, ᏃᏭᎴ Ꮎ ᏗᎳᏏᏗ - bases ᎤᎾᎢ ᏃᏭ ᏯᏃ--ᏯᏃᎰᎾ,Ꮣ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᎾ
segments.transliteration: igadi’nv, nowule na dilasidi - bases unai nowu yano--yanohona,da, tsigehv una
segments.translation: Some of them would drop the dirt by the bases.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Ꮭ--Ꮭ’Ᏺ--ᎯᎢ … ᏥᏧᏣ’Ꮽ ᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᎩᎶ ᏱᏥᏯᏛᏛᎲᏍᎬ ᎾᏛᏁᎲ ᏕᏥᏍᏕᎸᎲ’Ꮽ “Hey! Hey! Hey!” ᏱᎦᎵ,ᏍᏕᎳ, y’know ᏥᎲᏍᎬ ᎦᏓ,
segments.transliteration: tla--tla’yo--hii … tsitsutsa’wu gehv tla gilo yitsiyadvdvhvsgv nadvnehv detsisdelvhv’wu “Hey! Hey! Hey!” yigali,sdela, y’know tsihvsgv gada,
segments.translation: I was just a little boy, I wasn’t asking anybody anything, I was just helping them. “Hey! Hey!” they’d say. I was just helping put dirt on the bases. [laughs]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꮫ Ꮎ ᎣᏣᏝᏅᏢ ᏧᎾ,ᏓᏝ,Ꭼ ᏍᎩᎾ North Greasy ᏣᏃᎮᎰ … ᎤᎾ Dry Creek ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏧᏄᎩᏍᏛ ᏍᎩ ᏳᎾ,ᏛᏁ ᎨᎮ
segments.transliteration: na’dv na otsatlanvtlv tsuna,datla,gv sgina North Greasy tsanoheho … una Dry Creek nigohilv tsunugisdv sgi yuna,dvne gehe
segments.translation: My brothers would gather where they call North Greasy. Dry Creek would always accuse them of using medicine.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Oh, yeah! ᎠᏴ,’Ꮫ Bell-Ꭲ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎪᎢ ᏗᏢ, ᏍᏊ ᏫᏚᏄ’ᎢᏍᏛ ᏍᎩ ᏄᎾ,ᏛᏁ ᎨᎲ Ꮄ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, I mean, ᎤᏠᏱ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩ--ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏍᎩ ᏄᎾ,ᏛᏁ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: Oh, yeah! ayv,’dv Bell-i nigohilv goi ditlv, squu widunu’isdv sgi nuna,dvne gehv le’le yigi, I mean, utloyi squu sgi--nigada, sgi nuna,dvne dohv?
segments.translation: Oh, yeah! Also, at Bell, they would accuse Greasy of doing that. But really, they all did that, didn’t they?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᎮᎾ, ᏜᏱᎪ ᎠᏁᎯ, ᎤᏂᎷᏨ ᏍᎩ’Ꮽ ᏍᏊ ᏧᏄᎩᏍᏛ, ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩ ᎾᎾᏛᏁᎲ … ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᎾᎵ,ᏍᏕᎸ,ᏙᏗ, ᏭᏂᎩᏒ ᏧᎾ,Ꮣ-ᏧᎾ,ᏓᏂᏐᏗ ‘ᎨᏅ … ᎤᏂᏢᏅ ᏚᏂᏝᏩᏛ ᏳᎾ,ᏝᏅᏓᏕᎳ, ‘ᎸᏢ ᎠᏃᎰᎾ,ᏗᏍᎬ … ᏐᏁᎳᏚ - ᎧᏂᎩᏓ, ᏕᎨᏥᏠᏒ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ)
segments.transliteration: sawu yuwaga,da, hena, dlayigo anehi, unilutsv sgi’wu squu tsunugisdv, gehv sgi nanadvnehv … sgina unali,sdelv,dodi, wunigisv tsuna,da-tsuna,danisodi ‘genv … unitlvnv dunitlawadv yuna,tlanvdadela, ‘lvtlv anohona,disgv … soneladu - kanigida, degetsitlosv (uyetsi,sgv)
segments.translation: One time, a team from Jay came, and they were also accused of doing that. They went to their cemetery to get dirt for their medicine. They put some in their pockets, and when they had the chance, they would drop it on the ground. They got beat 19 – 0. [laughs]

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꮫ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ Ꮎ a Ke—Ketcher’Ꮫ Rocky Mt. ᏗᏢ, Ꮒ,ᏓᏳᎶᏒ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏗ, ᏂᎪᎯᎸ’Ꮕ, ᏳᏬᏝ, ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᎠᎵ,ᏍᏛᏡᏍᎬ, ᏱᎨᎮ … ᏙᏳ’ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏭ ᏱᏄᏛᎿ, ᏳᎦ,ᏙᏍᏛ, ᏥᎨᎲ … ᎪᎩ,ᏍᎬ’Ꮕ, … “Hey! Ꭰ’ᎥᏱ ᏗᏢ, ᏩᎴᏅᏏ, ᎤᎾ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏗ, ᎠᏭ, ᏗᎪᎩ,ᏍᎩ” ᏣᎾ,ᏗᎲ “ᏦᎳ,’Ꭱ Ꭼ,Ꮧ!” ᏣᎾ,ᏗᎲ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ)
segments.transliteration: na’dv ganvdadisgo na a Ke—Ketcher’dv Rocky Mt. ditlv, ni,dayulosv udvhisdi, nigohilv’nv, yuwotla, tsigehv tla squu ali,sdvtlusgv, yigehe … doyu’hena, awu yinudvhna, yuga,dosdv, tsigehv … gogi,sgv’nv, … “Hey! a’vyi ditlv, walenvsi, una udvhisdi, awu, digogi,sgi” tsana,dihv “tsola,’e gv,di!” tsana,dihv (uyetsi,sgv)
segments.translation: Also, I remember there was a Ketcher that came from Rocky Mt. He was an old man. He would sit there. And he was the type that would never sit. He would sit there and he’d be smoking and watching. They would tell each other, “Go stand in front of that old man! He’s smoking! He’s using tobacco!” [laughs]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: “Go talk to him!” [distract him]

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: “Go talk to him!” [distract him]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: “Go break up his medicine!”

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: “ᎭᏁᎵ,Ꮧ ᏨᏂ,ᏍᏗ Ꮎ ᎪᎩ,ᏍᏗ ᏥᎪᎩ,ᏍᏗ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᎮᎾ, y’know? (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᏂᎦᏓ,’Ꮫ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ
segments.transliteration: “haneli,di tsvni,sdi na gogi,sdi tsigogi,sdi (uyetsi,sgv) diniyotli, hena, y’know? (uyetsi,sgv) nigada,’dv ganvdadisgo sginana
segments.translation: “Go try to knock the pipe he’s smoking!” (laughs) Kids, y’know? (laughs) I remember all of that. (laughs)

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: We’re going to finish up, now.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: Alright.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎢᏂᏍᏆᏗᏍᎬ’Ꮓ … ᎯᎢ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏥᏄᏍᏗ, ᏥᏂᏬᏂᎯ, ‘Ꮩ ᏓᎦᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂ, ᎮᎵ?
segments.transliteration: inisquadisgv’no … hii tsalagi, tsinusdi, tsiniwonihi, ‘do dagali,stani, heli?
segments.translation: To finish with, the Cherokee language we’re speaking, what do you think is going to happen with it?

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Well … ᎠCᎢᎴ’Ꭵ ᎦᎶᏍᎬ ᎭᏗ? Well Ꮫ-ᏛᏲᎱᏏ,’Ꮫ ᎠᏴ, ᏗᎦᏛᏒ Ꭲ’ᎢᏃᎮᏢ ᏄᏓᎴ’Ꮫ ᎡᎮᏍᏗ, ᎯᎾᎾ ᏣᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᎠ, ᏃᏭ, ᎠᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᎠ ᏣᎳᎩ, … Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᏙᏳ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏚᎾ,ᏛᏒ ᏗᏢ, ᏳᎾᏅ,ᏖᏍᏗ, … Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᏱᎾᎾ,ᏛᏁᎠ, … ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, ᏓᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᎬ’Ꮽ ᎠᎾᎢ,
segments.transliteration: Well … aCile’v galosgv hadi? Well dv-dvyohusi,’dv ayv, digadvsv i’inohetlv nudale’dv ehesdi, hinana tsana,delo,quaa, nowu, ana,delo,quaa tsalagi, … tla hena, doyu, tsalagi, duna,dvsv ditlv, yunanv,tesdi, … tla hena, yinana,dvnea, … doyu, hena, dana,delo,quasgv’wu anai,
segments.translation: Well … are you saying as years go on? It’s going to die away. The way we all grew up and how we talked. The way they’re learning today is different. They’re learning Cherokee, but they won’t know what it was like to grow up in the language. They’re not living like that now. All they know is what they’re learning.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They won’t know what--

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: --what we know.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They won’t know it.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.translation: That’s what I think. How about you? Do you think the same?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏬᎯᏳ’Ꮫ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎨᏍᏗ, Ꮭ ᏍᎩᎾ,’Ᏺ ᎠᏴ, ᏥᏂᏬᏂᎯ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏯᏂᏬᏂᏍᎨᏍᏗ,
segments.transliteration: awohiyu’dv aniwonisgesdi, tla sgina,’yo ayv, tsiniwonihi, yusdi, yaniwonisgesdi,
segments.translation: I think they will be speaking it, but they won’t be speaking like how we are.

segments.speaker: randy-duncan
segments.text: Yeah, Ꮭ ᏳᎾᏅ,ᏖᏍᏗ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏌᎷᏱ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, … Ꭳ-Ꭳ’Ꭲ-Ꭳ’ᎢᏰᎢᏍᏛ Ꮻ-ᏫᏗᎩᏍᎬ ᏕᎦᏁᎶᏅ ᎠᎹᏳᎵ,Ꮧ, … ᏍᎩ’Ꮽ ᏃᏭ, Ꮭ ᏳᎾᏅ,ᏖᏍᏗ, ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, Ꮟ’ᎡᏲ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎨᏍᏗ, ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏓᎩᏍᏕᎸᎲ ᏓᎩᏲᎱᏎᎵ, ᎮᎾ, … ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏂᎦᏛᏁᎸᎾ, ᏱᎩ, ᎠᏴ,’Ꮕ, ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᏍᏊ ᏥᎩ, … ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏂᏧᏣ, ᎡᎵᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᎦᏥᏰᏲᏅ ᏔᎵ, ᎠᏂᏧᏣ, ᏓᎩᎧᎭ ᎡᎵᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᏳᎾᏅ,Ꮫ … ‘ᎠᎮᎾ, ᏍᏓᏱ-ᏍᏓᏱ ᎨᎰ … ᏗᎨᏲᏗ … ᏲᏁᎦ, ᏱᏍᏗᏁᎳ,
segments.transliteration: Yeah, tla yunanv,tesdi, yusdi, saluyi, gohu,sdi, … o-o’i-o’iyeisdv wi-widigisgv deganelonv amayuli,di, … sgi’wu nowu, tla yunanv,tesdi, sginana ‘ahena, si’eyo atsalagi, aniwonisgesdi, sgina, dagisdelvhv dagiyohuseli, hena, … gohu,sdi, nigadvnelvna, yigi, ayv,’nv, ayv, hena, squu tsigi, … ayv, hena, anitsutsa, elisdi, hena, gatsiyeyonv tali, anitsutsa, dagikaha elisdi, hena, yunanv,dv … ‘ahena, sdayi-sdayi geho … digeyodi … yonega, yisdinela,
segments.translation: They won’t know things that grow in the woods that we went and harvested. And playing by the water. They won’t know things like that, but they will be speaking Cherokee. That’s what’s going to help. We’re going to lose those things, if we don’t do anything about it. Even me. I should have taught my two boys. They might know it. But it’s hard to teach if you’re married to an English-speaking person.
